recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change ActivityDefinition's workgroup metadata to a non-existent Workflow group for this issue; any future resource ownership transfer should come from a new formal work-group/FM G decision.
issue_request: FHIR-11147 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 request to move ActivityDefinition from the Clinical Decision Support work group to the workflow work group because ActivityDefinition supports broader workflow, order, catalog, and collaboration use cases beyond decision support.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-11147. The Jira comment says ActivityDefinition was recategorized as Workflow by Lloyd's changes. The related applied issue FHIR-10683 was implemented in SVN 11382 / git bd1507dafa96568bf37503ff029bbabe8c3d8be2, which updated CDS resource workflow mappings and added ActivityDefinition prose identifying it as a FHIR Workflow definition resource; Lloyd's 6a96b06674a4d5b68f27d9dc43227505f3c703b1 later strengthened Workflow-module treatment of ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition.
additional_context: The final resolution did not approve a resource ownership transfer because Workflow was a task force rather than a working group that could own resources. Current source/fhir.ini actively builds ActivityDefinition, assigns it to cds, and defines no Workflow workgroup code. The ActivityDefinition StructureDefinition also carries structuredefinition-wg cds and publisher Clinical Decision Support, while the ActivityDefinition introduction and Workflow pages present ActivityDefinition from the workflow definition perspective. FHIR-11148, FHIR-11232, and FHIR-14447 are related final issues already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source matches the approved decision: CDS remains the responsible work group, and the documentation already presents ActivityDefinition as a Workflow definition resource.

related_jiras.note: Applied the broader decision that CDS resources should follow and declare Workflow patterns, including ActivityDefinition as a Definition resource. Not decided here because it covers a broader CDS resource set.
